Title: What Do Financial Markets Reveal about Global Warming
Author/s: Ronald J. Balvers; Xiaobing Zhao; W. A. Franke
Abstract: Financial market information can provide an objective assessment of expected losses due to global warming. In a Merton-type asset pricing model, with asset prices affected by changes in investment opportunities caused by global warming, the risk premium is significantly negative and growing over time, loadings for most assets are negative, and asset portfolios in more vulnerable industries have stronger negative loadings on the global warming factor. Required returns are 0.11 percent higher due to global warming, implying a present value loss of 4.18 percent of wealth. These costs complement and exceed previous estimates of the cost of global warming.

Title: GLOBAL WARMING
Source Title: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Abstract: Global warming is defined as the rise in the temperature of the earth’s surface, atmosphere, oceans due to increase in greenhouse gases. When the heat radiation emitted by sun, reaches the planet earth, a certain amount of the heat radiation is absorbed by the surface, atmosphere and oceans, and the remaining amount is released back into space, because of this the surface of the earth gets warmed up creating a favorable environment for the life on earth. But because of the presence of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere the heat radiation emitted by the earth into space gets trapped in the atmosphere, this behavior of gases is known as greenhouse effect. But due to offending human activities towards the environment in the past two centuries has increased the amount of greenhouse gas composition in the atmosphere leading to excessive trapping of heat, which has resulted in the serious problem of global warming. Increased composition of the greenhouse gases which is leading to global warming has resulted in drastic change in the climate in past few decades. This acceleration in the warmth of the atmospheric temperature was due to increased human activities which included burning fossil fuels like natural gas, petroleum products and charcoal since the time of industrial revolution. Cutting of trees by Humans i.e deforestation has also contributed to global warming. Greenhouse gases mainly constitute of carbon-di-oxide, methane, nitrous oxide, halocarbons and other harmful gases emitted by the industries. These gases trap the heat received from the sun in the earth’s atmosphere leading to rise in temperature along the surface of the earth. This increase in temperature leads to melting of glaciers and rise in sea level which floods away the low lying areas leading to catastrophic disasters. Though global warming has caused such traumatic disasters in the past few decades there still exits a misconception among the public that the global warming is a distant threat whereby its consequences would be felt only after decades from now. The global warming can be caused due to natural reasons as well as human activities. The global warming caused by natural phenomena include the rotation of earth around the sun and the increased intensity of sunlight cast on earth when it is closer to the sun, volcanic eruptions release excessive amount of carbon-di-oxide and ash into the atmosphere hence these greenhouse gases trap the heat radiation from the sun which eventually results in rise of the atmospheric temperature of the earth. Methane, which is also, one of the greenhouse gases is usually released from cattle dung, landfills, coal mining and petroleum products, has the capacity of trapping the heat radiation twenty times to that of carbon-di-oxide which ultimately leads to global warming.

Title: Global warming and the railways
Abstract: Because of the disregard for energy conservation in the UK rail industry for so long, improvement should be easy to achieve. The CO2 reduction in 1995/96 was achieved by carrying more passengers and by improving the generation mix of the electricity supply. Rolling stock needs to lose weight, but this can only be done on new trains. To achieve this, it is necessary to go back to first principles and look at acceleration; going up hills; overcoming rolling and wind resistance; lighting, heating and ventilation. With an electric train, regenerative braking helps to recover and reuse energy. Coasting using high technology to help the drivers decide when to ease up, without losing time is another energy saving option. Returning energy to the grid would cost money initially, and in the absence of a business case could be done altruistically or with government subsidy. Air conditioning with a wider band of acceptable temperatures for passengers and a re-think on window size and lighting could help too. Overall, electrification is the most effective solution tackling issues such as pollution, fuel availability, economy, performance, capacity, reliability and train maintenance.

Title: A Review on Global Warming

Abstract: <jats:p>One of the most important environmental issues of our time is global warming, which is primarily caused by human activity. In order to provide a thorough examination of the phenomenon, this review paper will cover its fundamental causes, observed and anticipated effects on the Earth's climate and ecosystems, as well as proposed mitigating measures. The atmospheric emission of greenhouse gases, particularly carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O), is the main cause of global warming. The remarkable rise in greenhouse gas concentrations during the past century has been mostly attributed to the burning of fossil fuels, deforestation, industrial operations, and agricultural activities. The effects of global warming are numerous and extensive. Increasing temperatures have sped up the melting of glaciers and polar ice caps, which has raised sea levels and increased the likelihood of coastal flooding. Extreme weather occurrences, such as heatwaves, droughts, and violent storms, have increased in frequency and have a negative effect on agriculture, water supplies, and vulnerable communities. Additionally, as ecosystems experience extraordinary shifts in temperature and precipitation patterns, biodiversity loss and ecosystem disruption are being seen. This paper presents a variety of potential mitigation tactics that could be used to alleviate the problems caused by global warming. Among these include switching to renewable energy sources, improving energy efficiency, putting reforestation and afforestation programmes into action, and applying sustainable agriculture methods. Additionally, international collaboration and policy frameworks are essential for promoting group initiatives. With significant effects on the environment and society, global warming continues to be a top priority. On a local, national, and international level, cooperation is required to address this complicated issue. This review emphasises how crucial it is to comprehend the underlying causes, effects, and mitigation strategies in order to effectively combat global warming and build a sustainable future for future generations</jats:p>

Title: Global Warming and Food Security in China
Abstract: Based on recent research of global warming's impact on crop productivity, this paper examines the effect of global warming on food security. Global warming will have negative effect on food security in China. Global warming as well as growing population, decreas of arable land and labour force will make the food security situation severe in China. Given the fact that global warming, growing population, decrease of arable land and labour force in China is irreversible, the increase of agricultural investment and technological progress are vital for food security in China. Global trade of grains will be changed by global warming, which means that a stable import source of grain for China is important.

Title: Driving Global Warming: Commuting in Maine and Its Contribution to Global Warming
Author/s: Mary Braun; Tony Dutzik; Matthew Davis; Pete Didisheim
Abstract: This report discusses how the state of Maine contributes to national global warming in the United States. It estimates that transportation is responsible for a little less than one third of the state's contribution to global warming, and work trips are a hefty portion of that contribution. The report analyzes which part of the state the commuters come from, discusses the types of residential development in the state, and provides suggestions for decreasing transportation related global warming. These suggestions include: decreasing single driver commutes; expanding the public transit network; encouraging home based telecommuting; encouraging residents to live near their places of work; encouraging carpooling; encouraging transit-oriented development and urban redevelopment; and encouraging residents to buy vehicles that produce less carbon dioxide.

Title: Global warming, a global energy resource
Abstract: <jats:p>Global warming is a thermodynamics problem. When excess heat is added to the climate system, the land warms more quickly than the oceans due to the land’s reduced heat capacity. The oceans have a greater heat capacity because of its higher specific heat and the heat mixing in the upper layer of the ocean. Thermodynamic Geoengineering (TG) is a global cooling method which deployed at scale would generate 1.6 times the world’s current supply of primary energy and remove carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere. The cooling would mirror the ostensible 2008–2013 global warming hiatus. At scale 31,000 1-gigawatt (GW) ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) plants are estimated to be able to: a) displace about 0.8 watts per square meter (W/m2) of average global surface heat from the surface of the ocean to deep water that could be recycled in 226-year cycles, b) produce 31 terawatts (TW) (relative to 2019 global use of 19.2 TW and c) absorb about 4.3 Gt CO2 per year from the atmosphere by cooling the surface. The estimated cost of these plants is $2.1 trillion per year or 30 years to ramp up to 31,000 plants which are replaced as needed thereafter. Compared for example to the cost of world oil consumption that in 2019 was $2.3 trillion for 11.6 TW. The cost of the energy generated is estimated at $0.008/KWh.</jats:p>
